report:
FRESH INDEPENDENT R4 SECURITY REVIEW (Opus 4.8, HIGH, tools read-only; second fresh context; the other current R4 vote is not in my packet and was not assumed).

SCOPE. Full source audit of the CURRENT reconstructed R4 builder contract/API (S36 contract 28131 B, S37 api/2 13080 B) and the exact 12 clause literals (S38), against CP consumer profile r2 revision 4 (S31 contract, S32 api/3), the root test-authoring readoption (S39), the Opus-4.8 routing note (S40), and the reconstruction delta (S41). I read the actual dependency source rather than trusting author claims: host_codec.py (S22), build_k10_inputs.py legacy (S24), the Sol renderer _render_prepared_outputs (S17) and its integration contract (S18), the R3 prefix (S12), and v1 c2_issue_artifacts.py (S23, head/labels/return). No execution, import, hashing, writing, shell, web, private or original-path follow; runtime behaviour below is prediction, not execution.

DEPENDENCY IDENTITY. Confirmed against source: (a) 16-entry r2 label map in S37 dependency.labels is byte-identical to S32 labels and CP §4 — expiry/context/policyId/trustProfile/setupRecordLink/groth16/vkCurveValidity/vkProfile/proofCurveValidity/statementReencode/jsonParseLimits/relationProfile/driverId/rustAcceptance/circuitVkCorrespondence/ledger. (b) 12 resultKeys in S37 exactly match the dict returned by v1 prepare_c2_issue (S23 lines 344-357): format, envData, envCborHex, envelopeTokenNameHex, issueData, issueCborHex, mintValueData, mintValueCborHex, policyIdHex, expiry, setupRecordSha256Declared, labels; CP06 preserves these 12 keys for r2 with only format→/2 and the 16 labels. (c) 11 C2I stages (ARG..BUILD) in S37/S32/CP match CB408. (d) v1 _LABELS (S23 lines 58-67) has exactly 8 entries, a strict subset; CB409 exact-dict equality against the 16-entry map therefore refuses the v1 8-entry map, the superseded 14-entry map and any missing/extra/changed entry. (e) No /2→/1 bridge: CB401 forbids importing/binding c2_issue_artifacts and forbids /2→/1 bridging; v1 stays unimported and absent from the envelope.

BRIDGE / HOST-ENCODING SUBSTANCE (CB409/CB410). I verified the CBOR-equality claims directly. host_codec.build_env_data (S24→S22 lines 621-641) returns the 9-node ('constr',0,[('int',2),('int',0),('bytes',FAMILY_V2),('bytes',predicate),('bytes',vk),('bytes',claimant),('constr',0,[('bytes',txid),('int',idx)]),('bytes',stmt),('int',expiry)]), which is exactly the tuple legacy_env_from_host admits per contract §5. host_codec._encode and legacy.cbor_encode produce identical bytes for these shapes: both use definite maps (0xa0 vs _cbor_head(5,·)), identical constr-tag mapping (index 0 → 121 → 0xd8 0x79), indefinite arrays (0x9f…0xff) for non-empty children, and identical int/bytes heads for the ≤32-byte leaves used here; legacy's >64-byte fail-closed path and host's indefinite-chunk path are not reached for the env/value rows. build_value_data(None,[(policy,token,1)]) and legacy.value_map yield equal CBOR for the 28-byte policy and 32-byte token. issueData=('constr',0,[('bytes',vk),('bytes',proof)]) with vk 488 / proof 192 is host-only because legacy.cbor_encode raises ValueError above 64 bytes (S24 lines 244-248) — the contract's HOST_ONLY_LEGACY_CANNOT_ENCODE_OVER_64_BYTES label is accurate. These builder re-derivations mirror v1/r2's own BUILD computation (S23 lines 329-343) field-for-field, so CB409's equalities both hold for a genuine r2 output and detect any drift. CB407 policy derivation matches legacy.extract_compiled / recompute_script_hash exactly (blake2b-224(0x03‖code), 56 hex, PIN_B9_APPLIED present). The renderer (S17) and its integration contract (S18) confine Sol to mechanical rendering after Opus discharges every precondition, consistent with CB410.

PREFIX IMPLEMENTABILITY. The R3 prefix (S12) demonstrates parse_expiry/read_public_file/parse_public_json/check_setup_link are implementable to the stated shapes. Note that read_public_file must be REWRITTEN for R4, not reused verbatim: the R3 version converts fstat/read OSErrors to C2B-READ and lacks the advisory no-follow lstat and O_NOCTTY that CB405 now requires (map only lstat/open errno; propagate fstat/read/close OSError). Section 0 already restricts reuse to text that satisfies the clause, so this is implementation guidance, not a contract conflict.

NON-CLAIMS. CB412 and the labels correctly claim nothing about Groth16, VK/proof curve validity, VK profile, statement re-encode, Rust parse_json limits, circuit/VK correspondence, Rust acceptance (no subset/equivalence/conditional-inclusion), or the ledger; driverId stays DECLARED_NAME_NOT_PROVENANCE, circuitVkCorrespondence OPEN, setup class-0 single-party TEST ONLY and forgeable, caller context unauthenticated, expiry caller-supplied and not proof-bound. All 20 UTxO families, general financial/residual, recursion, private handoff and multiparent remain open. No native/VM/proof/ledger authority is granted.

VOTES. Independent substantive AGREE on all twelve clauses CB401–CB412, including the two reworded clauses needing fresh votes (CB409 16-entry map and refusals; CB412 added non-claims and CP08-gated reliance). I found no DISAGREE-worthy defect: the contract is internally coherent and implementable as the basis for separately-reviewed R4 test authoring.

GATING. The r2 implementation c2_issue_artifacts_r2.py is absent and not root-adopted (S39 adopts the CP policy for TEST AUTHORING ONLY; builderReliancePermitted false, nativeAuthority 0). Therefore meaningful R00/RED cannot yet pass (R00 requires root-adopted r2 bytes), no tests are authored, and GREEN/builder reliance stay unreached. sourceReady=true strictly as a basis for separately-reviewed R4 test authoring with the r2 adoption dependency still pending; this is one vote of the two substantively-agreeing votes needed for any consequential decision and is not itself adoption. Same-provider context independence only; no provider diversity claimed.

findings.evidence: S12 read_public_file/_read_regular_fd convert fstat and os.read OSErrors to 'C2B-READ: ...' (S12 lines 62, 71) and omit the advisory no-follow lstat and O_NOCTTY. CB405 (S36/S38) requires a no-follow lstat S_ISREG precheck, O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOCTTY, mapping ONLY the listed lstat/open errno classes to C2B-READ, and letting every fstat/read/close OSError propagate unconverted after a best-effort close.
findings.requiredFix: The fresh R4 prefix must re-author read_public_file to CB405; the R3 body is NOT reusable verbatim. Test review must assert fstat/read/close OSErrors propagate (not C2B-READ) and that the lstat/O_NOCTTY precheck exists. Contract-consistent; section 0 permits reuse only where it satisfies the clause.

findings.evidence: CB409 (S36/S38) names build_env_data inputs as export 'predicateDigest, vkDigestBlake2b256, ... statementDigestBlake2b256', while the admitted export's cardano.envV2 uses keys vkDigest/statementDigest (S23 lines 305-315). v1 cross-checks these equal (context digest == header digest == envV2.statementDigest; S23 lines 283-295, 326), so either source yields byte-identical env CBOR.
findings.requiredFix: None at contract level. The R4 implementation and test author must fix which export field the builder reads for each env node and confirm it equals the envV2 value, so the CB409 re-derivation is unambiguous.

findings.evidence: S37 prerequisites list c2_issue_artifacts_r2.py as 'exact reviewed and root-adopted bytes; bytes and SHA-256 from the root adoption record', but S39 adopts the CP policy for TEST AUTHORING ONLY (implementationAdopted false, testExecutionPermittedByThisRecord false, builderReliancePermitted false, nativeAuthority 0); no r2 implementation, bytes, SHA-256, RED or GREEN exists. R00 (S36 §7) requires the root-adopted r2.
findings.requiredFix: None; this is the correct firstBlockedBoundary. Meaningful R4 RED requires a root-adopted, reviewed r2; CP08 r2 reliance decision, reviewed r2 implementation, fresh non-author Opus audit + Muse Sol review, and RED→GREEN all remain open. sourceReady is bounded to test-authoring basis only.

findings.evidence: I confirmed legacy.cbor_encode and host_codec.encode_data agree for the frozen env/value shapes (all leaves <=32 bytes; S22 lines 30-139 vs S24 lines 238-264). They diverge generally: legacy fails closed on >64-byte byte strings (S24 244-248) whereas host chunks indefinitely (S22 38-43); legacy has no map/visit bound whereas host enforces _MAX_VISITS=65536.
findings.requiredFix: None. CB409 correctly scopes the legacy/host CBOR-equality to the specific T1/T5/T6/T7 env and value rows; the issue payload is explicitly host-only. The claim must not be read as a general encoder equivalence, and the contract does not so read it.

findings.evidence: CB412/S37 manifest asserts 'exactly the 33-key MANIFEST_KEYS set of R3 test_c2_builder.py' and the 9 builderLabels / 4 limitations / 10 flags counts. The clause literals do not enumerate the 33 keys inline, and S16 test_c2_builder.py was not read in this review.
findings.requiredFix: Non-blocking for the clause vote. A later test-authoring review must pin the 33 MANIFEST_KEYS literally from S16 and confirm the builder manifest carries exactly them plus the 16 consumerLabels, 9 builderLabels, 4 limitations and 10 false flags, with no manifest string containing 'subset' (R13).

positions.clause: The builder shall be a new file build_k10_inputs_r4.py, consisting of a new R4 prefix ending in the line `# === C2B-R4-APPEND-SEAM: append tail below; prefix above is immutable ===` and a tail, whose only import statements are import hashlib, import json, import os, import re, import stat, import sys, import build_k10_inputs as legacy, import c2_issue_artifacts_r2 and import host_codec, which exposes exactly parse_expiry, read_public_file, parse_public_json, check_setup_link, legacy_env_from_host, plan_outputs and main, which calls c2_issue_artifacts_r2.prepare_c2_issue and host_codec APIs by module attribute at call time, and which never imports or binds the identifier c2_issue_artifacts, mutates sys.path or sys.modules, uses importlib, rebinds an imported module or attribute, or bridges format /2 to /1.
positions.rationale: The nine-import, seven-public-name shape matches the demonstrated R3 prefix (S12) with v1 swapped for c2_issue_artifacts_r2; the versioned append-seam keeps v1 (S23) unimported and absent from the envelope, and by-attribute calls preserve the no-rebind rule. The /2->/1 non-bridge is consistent with v1's 8-label format/1 being a strict subset refused at CB409.

positions.clause: Where any public function is called, the builder shall promise behaviour only for exact builtin arguments (str, bytes, int that is not bool, an exact list argv, and dicts returned by parse_public_json or first proven to have only exact str keys), shall invoke no caller-defined hook (subclass, PathLike, __fspath__, __index__, __eq__ or __hash__) before refusing, and shall raise every refusal as a ValueError with one exact str argument `C2B-<STAGE>: <reason>` on one line, where reason is a fixed literal optionally carrying a module constant, an errno class name and number, or, for CONSUMER only, a conforming C2I message, so that no path, argv text or other caller free text is echoed.
positions.rationale: The R3 prefix (S12) shows type(x) is checks, _os_reason emitting only class name and errno, and no caller text in refusals, so the exact-builtin / no-hook / no-echo discipline is implementable as written and resolves the F06/F07 echo and hook concerns without dependency impact.

positions.clause: When main(argv) is called, the builder shall refuse C2B-ARGV before any filesystem access unless type(argv) is list, len(argv) == 6 in the order prog b9-applied.json proof-export.json setup-record.json expiry-ms output-dir, every element is an exact str, argv[1], argv[2], argv[3] and argv[5] are each non-empty, NUL-free and accepted by os.fsencode (UnicodeEncodeError caught without echo), and parse_expiry admits argv[4] as an exact str fully matching ASCII (?:0|[1-9][0-9]{0,19}) with value <= 2**64-1, with no default, clock, environment or TEST_EXPIRY fallback.
positions.rationale: parse_expiry in S12 already fullmatches the exact ASCII decimal and bounds to 2**64-1 with no fallback, superseding legacy's TEST_EXPIRY constant (S24 line 95). Pre-refusing before any filesystem access, with fsencode UnicodeEncodeError caught and not echoed, is coherent and strictly ordered.

positions.clause: When ARGV passes, the builder shall refuse C2B-OUTDIR, creating nothing, unless os.path.split(argv[5]) gives a basename fully matching ASCII [a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,99}, the parent ("." when empty) opens with O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC as a directory fd that main keeps as the pinned parent until it returns, and os.stat(basename, dir_fd=parent, follow_symlinks=False) fails with ENOENT, treating only the final component as no-follow and parent-path symlinks as the caller's trust.
positions.rationale: Pinning the parent by an O_DIRECTORY fd and requiring the no-follow basename stat to fail ENOENT closes the create-time rebinding race while creating nothing on refusal. The final-component-only no-follow policy is explicit and the basename regex admits realistic operator names (e.g. the legacy EXPECTED_OUTPUT_BASENAME).

positions.clause: When OUTDIR passes, main shall read argv[1], argv[2] and argv[3] in that order with read_public_file and the caps 16777216, 1048576 and 65536, and read_public_file(path, cap) shall refuse C2B-READ unless path is an exact non-empty NUL-free fsencode-encodable str, cap is one of those three constants, a no-follow lstat reports S_ISREG, os.open(os.fsencode(path), O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOCTTY) succeeds, fstat of that fd reports S_ISREG, and os.read chunks of at most 65536 bytes until EOF or cap+1 total bytes give at most cap bytes, closing the fd on every path, mapping only the listed lstat/open errno classes to C2B-READ and letting every other OSError (including any from fstat, read or close), MemoryError, OverflowError and KeyboardInterrupt propagate unconverted after a best-effort close.
positions.rationale: The bounded cap+1 read, advisory no-follow lstat, authoritative fstat, O_NOCTTY and explicit errno split are coherent and distinguish input verdicts from resource failures. Finding R4-F01 notes the R3 body must be re-authored (it wrongly converts fstat/read errno and lacks lstat/O_NOCTTY), which is implementation guidance, not a contract defect; the clause text itself is correct.

positions.clause: When plan_outputs(b9_raw, export_raw, setup_raw, expiry) runs, it shall first refuse C2B-ARGV unless type(expiry) is int and 0 <= expiry <= 2**64-1, then refuse C2B-JSON for the export (cap 1048576) and then the setup (cap 65536) unless parse_public_json admits exact bytes no longer than cap, without a UTF-8 BOM, decoding as strict UTF-8 to exactly one top-level object with only space, tab, LF or CR before and after it, no raw control character in a string, no duplicate key after unescaping at any depth, no NaN, Infinity, fraction or exponent, every integer literal fully matching ASCII (?:0|-?[1-9][0-9]*) in at most 20 characters counting the sign (so -0 is refused), no lone surrogate in any key or string, and at most 16 nesting levels counting the top-level object as 1, enforced by a lexical pre-scan before decoding and a post-walk, with RecursionError and decode errors mapped to C2B-JSON and no JSON canonicality claimed beyond exact-byte SHA-256 identity.
positions.rationale: The S12 parse_public_json implements the BOM, strict-UTF-8, duplicate-key, parse_float/parse_constant rejection, 20-char signed-int, surrogate and lexical depth pre-scan plus post-walk exactly, with RecursionError and other ValueErrors mapped to C2B-JSON. The clause correctly frames this as the builder's own gate, distinct from Rust parse_json, with jsonParseLimits staying NOT_CHECKED and no canonicality beyond SHA-256 identity.

positions.clause: When JSON passes, plan_outputs shall refuse C2B-LINK unless every key of the export is an exact str and export setupRecordSha256 is an exact str fully matching ASCII [0-9a-f]{64} equal to hashlib.sha256(setup_raw).hexdigest(), and shall then refuse C2B-POLICY unless b9_raw is exact bytes of at most 16777216 bytes whose SHA-256 equals legacy.PIN_B9_APPLIED before legacy.extract_compiled is called, the unchanged extract_compiled returns (code_hex, policy_hex) without ValueError, policy_hex is 56 lowercase hex, and hashlib.blake2b(bytes([3]) + bytes.fromhex(code_hex), digest_size=28).hexdigest() == policy_hex, using those 28 bytes as policy_id; the pin is wrapper integrity, not program admission.
positions.rationale: legacy.PIN_B9_APPLIED exists (S24 line 58) and extract_compiled returns (code_hex, recomputed 28-byte hash as 56 hex) via recompute_script_hash = blake2b-224(0x03||code) (S24 lines 168-180, 397-430), matching the clause byte-for-byte. Checking the SHA-256 pin before extract_compiled ensures only pinned bytes reach legacy parsing, and the clause correctly scopes the file-byte link to one builder run with no Rust-acceptance claim.

positions.clause: When POLICY passes, plan_outputs shall call c2_issue_artifacts_r2.prepare_c2_issue(export, setup, expiry, policy_id=policy) exactly once and, if it raises ValueError, shall refuse with `C2B-CONSUMER: ` followed by the message when the exception has exactly one exact str argument of at most 1024 characters, without CR or LF, beginning `C2I-<STAGE>: ` for a STAGE in ARG, SETUP, PROFILE, EXPORT, RELATION, STATEMENT, CONTEXT, DIGEST, PROOF, CARDANO or BUILD, and otherwise with `C2B-CONSUMER: nonconforming consumer refusal` without echo, letting every non-ValueError exception propagate.
positions.rationale: The CP r2 contract (S31 CP07) guarantees exactly ValueError with a C2I-<STAGE>: prefix over the same 11 stages (S32 stages), so the builder's conforming-message set and 1024-char/CR-LF bound are well-defined. Wrapping a conforming message and collapsing anything else to the fixed literal without echo, while non-ValueError propagates, is coherent and single-call.

positions.clause: When CONSUMER returns, plan_outputs shall refuse C2B-BRIDGE unless the result is an exact dict with exactly the 12 API resultKeys; format is exactly moriarty-c2-issue-artifacts/2; labels is an exact dict equal to the frozen 16-entry r2 label map of API dependency.labels, so that the v1 8-entry map, the superseded 14-entry map and any missing, extra or changed entry are refused; policyIdHex == policy.hex(), expiry is an exact int equal to the argument, and setupRecordSha256Declared equals the LINK digest; every *Hex value is an exact even-length lowercase hex str; envData equals host_codec.build_env_data over predicateDigest, vkDigestBlake2b256, context claimantVkh, consumedTxid, consumedIx and statementDigestBlake2b256 of the admitted export and expiry, legacy_env_from_host admits it, and legacy.cbor_encode of the translation, host_codec.encode_data(envData) and bytes.fromhex(envCborHex) are equal, with BLAKE2b-256 of them equal to envelopeTokenNameHex; mintValueData equals host_codec.build_value_data(None, [(policy, token, 1)]) and legacy.cbor_encode(legacy.value_map(policy, token, 1)), host_codec.encode_data(mintValueData) and bytes.fromhex(mintValueCborHex) are equal; issueData is exactly ('constr', 0, [('bytes', vk), ('bytes', proof)]) with exact types, vk the 488 setup VK bytes and proof the 192 export proof bytes, equal to host_codec.build_c2_mint_data('Issue', vk, proof), and host_codec.encode_data(issueData) == bytes.fromhex(issueCborHex), host-only because the legacy encoder fails closed above 64 bytes; and the T7 legacy env CBOR equals host_codec.encode_data of build_env_data with legacy.flip_first_bit(vk digest).
positions.rationale: Reworded clause verified against source: the frozen 16-entry map equals S32/CP §4; v1's _LABELS is exactly 8 entries (S23 58-67) so exact-dict equality refuses it and the superseded 14-entry map and any drift. build_env_data's 9-node tuple (S22 621-641) is exactly what legacy_env_from_host admits, and legacy.cbor_encode vs host.encode_data produce identical CBOR for these <=32-byte-leaf shapes (definite maps, 0xd879 constr-0 tag, indefinite arrays). issueData is host-only because legacy.cbor_encode raises above 64 bytes (S24 244-248) while vk=488/proof=192 pass host _data_bytes. Every re-derivation mirrors v1/r2's own BUILD (S23 329-343), so the equalities catch any drift. Fresh independent vote recorded.

positions.clause: When BRIDGE passes, plan_outputs shall construct exactly the rows T1 (consumer env, consumer token, quantity 1), T5 (quantity 2), T6 (legacy.flip_first_bit of the token) and T7 (env with flipped vk digest and its recomputed token), all with the genuine VK and proof, compute each row's envelopeCborHex, tokenNameHex, quantity, envVkDigestHex, envStatementDigestHex and proofHexSha256 itself, assemble every other manifest field from the frozen API literals and the checked values, call the verbatim Sol helper _render_prepared_outputs only after all of this, and return its fresh dict of exactly the 6 API relpaths to bytes, with T2-T4 only as coverageGaps and no I/O, clock, randomness or environment access.
positions.rationale: The Sol renderer (S17) is purely mechanical: it unpacks four rows, calls legacy.script_context and legacy.uplc_term, copies the six Opus-computed metadata fields and manifest scalars, and returns a fresh six-entry dict with no host encoder, hash, consumer, I/O or mutation (S18 confirms the precondition ownership). legacy.flip_first_bit exists (S24 433-434) for the T6/T7 mutations, and the four IDs match the renderer constants, so Opus-owned construction before a verbatim render is coherent, with T2-T4 left as gaps.

positions.clause: When planning succeeds, main shall create the output with os.mkdir(basename, 0o755, dir_fd=parent) and contexts with os.mkdir("contexts", 0o755, dir_fd=out), pinning each by an O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC fd, write script.hex and then the T1, T5, T6 and T7 contexts each through os.open(name, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOCTTY, 0o644, dir_fd=pinned) with a complete os.write loop and close, re-read the three inputs with read_public_file and the same caps refusing C2B-REREAD on any refusal or byte difference, write manifest.json.tmp the same way and publish it last by os.rename to manifest.json within the pinned output fd, print exactly one JSON line {"output": argv[5], "cases": 4} and return 0, mapping every OSError while creating, writing, closing or publishing to C2B-WRITE; after the first mkdir, any refusal or exception shall first trigger cleanup of exactly the entries this call created (unlink files, rmdir contexts, rmdir output, all by pinned dir fd, OSError ignored), and every refusal at any stage shall print exactly one stderr line, no stdout, and return 2, while non-refusal exceptions propagate.
positions.rationale: Exclusive O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW creates through pinned dir fds, a complete write loop, a REREAD byte-equality check with the same caps, and a last os.rename publish give an atomic manifest that exists only when the output is complete. Cleanup limited to this call's own created entries through pinned fds, with one stderr line / exit 2 on any C2B- refusal and propagation otherwise, is a sound and implementable effect/exception map (stronger than legacy S24's non-atomic writes).

positions.clause: The builder and manifest shall claim nothing about Groth16, VK or proof curve validity, VK profile, statement re-encode, Rust parse_json limits, circuit/VK correspondence, Rust acceptance of any admitted input (including any subset, equivalence or conditional-inclusion relation), the ledger or provider, fees, min-ADA, collateral, ExUnits, fit, Preview, Preprod or operator compatibility, and shall infer none of these from the r2 descriptor checks or the builder's own gates; shall carry the frozen builderLabels, limitations and the 16 r2 consumerLabels, label the context FABRICATED_LOCAL_VM_TEST, the expiry caller-supplied and not proof-bound, the declared context unauthenticated and the setup single-party TEST ONLY and forgeable; and shall keep every flag and builderReliancePermitted false, which may change only by a separate root source-adoption decision taken after the CP08 root decision for the reviewed r2, a fresh review of this contract, a reviewed R4 implementation, a fresh non-author Opus audit with a Muse review of the Sol glue, and root-observed meaningful RED then GREEN all exist, none of which grants it automatically.
positions.rationale: Reworded clause aligns with CP r2 (S31/S32 labels: rustAcceptance NOT_ESTABLISHED, vkProfile and jsonParseLimits NOT_CHECKED, circuitVkCorrespondence OPEN) and with S39, which adopts CP for test authoring only with builderReliancePermitted false and nativeAuthority 0. Adding VK profile, Rust parse_json limits and every Rust-acceptance relation to the non-claims, forbidding inference from descriptor checks, and gating reliance on CP08 plus the full prerequisite chain with nothing automatic is correct and conservative. Fresh independent vote recorded.
